cards.title: Four rings
cards.text: Device, campus, VSU-wide, and the internet. Each ring is meant to keep working when the rings outside it fail.

claims.text: What VSU makes would live on VSU's own network and servers first, with the internet as the outer ring, still open for everything from outside.
VSU has already built a fiber backbone, Wi-Fi across most of the Main Campus, and a typhoon-hardened data center on solar backup.
The campus intranet is a direction, not an ask.

cards.title: A question finds its answer
cards.text: In the network, a question would go to the office or person who can answer it. The confirmed answer would stay, dated and findable, and every notice would show who stands behind it.

claims.text: The network is built for three jobs: routing, memory, and trust.
In the network's design, questions are routed, not broadcast, and move to the office responsible when only an office can settle them.

cards.title: Wi-Fi access points
cards.text: In the campus-first design, access points would sit on each building's switches, sized for the people in a room, with sign-in by university account. Being on campus Wi-Fi alone would grant no trust.

claims.text: Access points would be sized by how many people use a space, with sign-in by university account.
Verified when accessed: every service checks who is asking, on campus or off.

cards.title: Switch and fiber
cards.text: In the campus-first design, the building's switch would join its access points to the fiber backbone, which runs to the data center at the campus core.

claims.text: VSU finished a new fiber backbone in 2017, after Typhoon Haiyan destroyed most of the old one in 2013.
Two fiber paths to each major building, so one cut does not isolate it.
The backbone's layout and redundancy are not public.

cards.title: Every post says what it is
cards.text: Official, community knowledge, opinion, unverified, scholarly, or external. In the network's design, only offices in official spaces post as official, and a notice shows whether it is current, updated, superseded, or archived.

claims.text: Every post carries one of six information types, and notices show whether they are current, updated, superseded, or archived.

cards.title: Kept for the next batch
cards.text: In the network's design, confirmed answers, guides, and notices stay, dated and findable. Discussion fades on a published schedule.

claims.text: The network keeps knowledge and lets conversation fade.
Because every kept answer makes the next question easier, the network's value compounds over the years.

cards.title: Saved on this phone
cards.text: The innermost ring would be the phone itself: it would keep the latest notices, so they open with no connection.

claims.text: A phone out of coverage still shows the notices it last synced.

cards.title: Scenes to come
cards.text: The problem scenes will sit here, at a kind of place. They are drawn next, and VSU evidence for them is still to come.

claims.text: A problem sits at a kind of place, never a named building or office, until VSU evidence ties it there.

scenes.title: One campus, two layers
scenes.summary: The intranet on the ground: what VSU makes would live on VSU's own network first. The network above it: a question would reach someone who can answer, and the answer would stay.

claims.text: CAMPUS proposes a digital layer over the physical university, connecting its people, places, knowledge, and services.
One product, the social/academic network, with a campus intranet as its long-term infrastructure.

scenes.title: Inside an academic building
scenes.summary: Rooms and a hall. In the campus-first design, each has Wi-Fi access points on the building's switch, joined by fiber to the campus core.

claims.text: VSU finished a new fiber backbone in 2017, after Typhoon Haiyan destroyed most of the old one in 2013.
Access points on each building's switches, joined by fiber to the campus core.

scenes.title: A computer lab
scenes.summary: A whiteboard, tables and chairs, computers, and on one screen, the network: a department's community, open between tasks.

claims.text: The network is built first for the academic side of university life, with campus life around it.
Its communities are tied to real units, such as a department, each with a named owner.

scenes.title: The network, on a computer
scenes.summary: A department's community: an office notice labeled official and current, and a question with a confirmed answer, kept for the next batch.

claims.text: The first build is a small prototype of the network on made-up data.
Made-up content is marked as made up wherever it appears.

scenes.title: Between classes
scenes.summary: Outside the building, between classes, a student checks the same community on a phone.

claims.text: Outdoor access points where people gather, and wireless bridges where fiber cannot reach.

scenes.title: The same network, on a phone
scenes.summary: The same notice and the same kept answer, with the latest notices saved on the phone for when the signal drops.

claims.text: The first build is a small prototype of the network on made-up data.
A phone out of coverage still shows the notices it last synced.
